answer.text: Short-lived branches merged often into one shared trunk.

cards.summary: Delivery is on demand; deployment is automatic

prompt.text: What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?

answer.text: Delivery ships on demand; deployment ships automatically.

options: Delivery ships on demand; deployment ships automatically
correct: Delivery ships on demand; deployment ships automatically

hints: One still has a human release button.

teaching.text: Continuous delivery keeps every change releasable and leaves the release decision to a person. Continuous deployment removes that button and releases every passing change.

teaching.text: Staging is only useful if it resembles production in configuration and scale. Real customer data must not be copied there without a privacy process.

teaching.text: Rollback may mean redeploying the previous artifact, flipping a flag or reversing a migration. Decide which before the release, not during the incident.
